items.title: File Widerspruch against partial refusal of plastic window frames
items.quote: Binnen eines Monats ab der Bekanntgabe dieses Bescheids ist der Widerspruch zulässig; er wird schriftlich oder zur Niederschrift bei folgender Stelle erhoben: Hansestadt Beispielwismar, Am Markt 1, 23966 Beispielwismar.
items.computation: Bescheiddatum (and presumed posting date) is Thursday 19.11.2026. The letter states the decision is deemed notified on the 'vierten Tag' (fourth day) after posting, but the applicable statutory rule (§ 41 Abs. 2 VwVfG M-V, mirroring § 41 Abs. 2 Satz 1 VwVfG) provides for the THIRD day after posting as the fiction of notification (Bekanntgabe), not the fourth. Applying the correct statutory third-day rule: 19.11.2026 + 3 days = Sunday 22.11.2026 = deemed Bekanntgabe (this fictional notification date is not shifted for falling on a Sunday, as it is not itself a 'Frist' subject to § 193 BGB). The one-month Widerspruchsfrist then runs under § 31 VwVfG in conjunction with §§ 187 Abs. 1, 188 Abs. 2 BGB: the day of the event (22.11.2026) is not counted, and the period ends on the day of the following month bearing the same number as the day of the event, i.e. 22.12.2026. 22.12.2026 is a Tuesday and not a public holiday in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, so no further shift under § 193 BGB is needed. (Note: if one instead used the letter's own, legally inaccurate, 'fourth day' rule, Bekanntgabe would fall on 23.11.2026 and the deadline on 23.12.2026; the earlier, legally correct date of 22.12.2026 is used here as the safer/earliest plausible deadline.)

warnings: The letter's stated delivery-fiction rule ('gilt am vierten Tag nach der Aufgabe zur Post als bekannt gegeben') does not match the actual wording of § 41 Abs. 2 VwVfG (and its M-V equivalent), which specifies the THIRD day after posting, not the fourth; the Widerspruch deadline has been computed using the legally correct third-day rule (yielding the earlier, safer date of 22.12.2026) — you may want to double-check this with the authority or a legal adviser, since relying on the letter's own (later) date could risk missing the real deadline.
The exact date the letter was actually handed to the postal service is assumed to be the same as the printed Bescheiddatum (19.11.2026); if it was posted later, the deadline shifts accordingly.
